items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: We gave a party at Max and Betty Jones' home for the Bruce Turner gang, and a few intimate friends.

ctx.x: Many of the places we played were small towns but we always had a swinging full house. Bruce and the boys really pushed me and I found out that Bruce was very popular everywhere he went. The Harold Davison office was satisfied with the results of the successful reports they received about the tour. So was I, and also to have seen the dream of my friend Ronald Sweetman come true in the form of me making a tour in that great jazz loving country.

We gave a party at Max and Betty Jones' home for the Bruce Turner gang, and a few intimate friends. Max had been a well known critic and reporter for the Melody Maker musical magazine for many years. Bruce and the boys had a surprise gift for me which was a silver beer mug ingraved: "To Bill - the Guv'nor" from Bruce, Pete, Tony, Ray, Ron and Doug. That was a real sender for me and a gift I shall always cherish. Being called 'Guv'nor' in England is an honour in most cases, and these fellows were honouring me.

Then we went to visit for a few days our friends Ronald Sweetman and his wife Jennifer in a beautiful little town called Steyning in the Sussex country. Jennifer, by the way, is a very well known artist who paints under her maiden name of Jennifer Dickson. Their house was called 'Ellington house'. I hope you know why! We had a swell time, and Jennifer and Ronald gave a party in our honour with 60 guests.
